rationale: New sourced discrepancy on the slow Accept path. handlePreAcceptReply acts on a reply carrying a higher ballot than the coordinator's: it increments lb.nacks and, once a majority nacks and the replica is the leader, calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870). handleAcceptReply has the analogous block but it is unreachable: the preceding guard returns whenever lb.lastTriedBallot != areply.Ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026), so the following test areply.Ballot > lb.lastTriedBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035) can never be true. Consequently an Accept reply that reports a higher ballot (handleAccept replies with inst.bal, epaxos/epaxos.go:1001-1004) is silently dropped: no nack is counted, the coordinator's ballot is not raised, and no Prepare is issued. A coordinator stuck at its Accept ballot then cannot assemble acceptOKs+1 > N/2 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1040) and the instance can only progress through the executeCommands recovery timer. I am raising this as a Candidate rather than a claimed defect because the stall may be bounded by that timer and the legality of a concurrent higher-ballot AcceptReply is not yet sourced.

feedback.answered: The higher-ballot handling on the Accept reply path is dead: handleAcceptReply returns on any ballot mismatch before its greater-than test, so a reply reporting a higher ballot is dropped without a nack, a ballot raise, or a Prepare, unlike the equivalent PreAccept reply path which does escalate. The remaining question is whether this can stall an instance long enough to matter, given the executeCommands recovery timer.
remaining: Whether a higher-ballot AcceptReply can legally arrive while the coordinator is in ACCEPTED status at its own ballot (concurrent recovery of the same instance).
Whether the resulting non-completion is bounded by the executeCommands COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD recovery timer in all cases.
Whether the IsLeader gating on the PreAccept path means a non-leader coordinator has no escalation route at all in either path.
A1 fast-path qualification and A2 ballot/authority transitions still have no executed check; membership (A4) and durability (A6) remain unread.
feedback.rationale: Records a concrete, sourced asymmetry between two structurally parallel reply handlers and keeps the boundedness and legality premises explicit instead of presuming a defect.

question.question: When a coordinator's Accept replies report a higher ballot than lb.lastTriedBallot, does the coordinator ever escalate (count a nack, raise its ballot, issue Prepare), or are those replies dropped so the instance stalls until the recovery timer?
question.importance: Progress of the slow Accept path: a coordinator that cannot learn about a higher ballot from Accept replies may be unable to complete the instance at its ballot, leaving progress dependent on the executeCommands recovery timer. This is a liveness concern, not a claim that a decided value can be corrupted.
participants: coordinator in ACCEPTED status for the instance
acceptor replying with a higher instance ballot
contexts: slow path after the fast quorum disagreed, so the coordinator broadcast Accept
concurrent recovery of the same instance at a higher ballot
event_paths: handleAcceptReply: equality guard (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) -> unreachable greater-than block (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035)
contrast: handlePreAcceptReply greater-than block -> makeBallot + bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870)

supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER: shows the intent to escalate on a higher ballot on the structurally parallel fast path
supporting_behavior_ids.B-RECOVERY-START: is the escalation target (makeBallot + bcastPrepare) that the Accept path never invokes
supporting_behavior_ids.B-EXEC: is the recovery timer that may bound the stall

counterevidence: The greater-than block is structurally redundant: the preceding guard returns whenever lb.lastTriedBallot != areply.Ballot, so no comparison against lastTriedBallot can be true afterwards.

The higher-ballot information is not wholly lost: the acceptor replied with inst.bal, and executeCommands enqueues recovery for a non-advancing instance after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, so the stall may be bounded.
handlePreAcceptReply does act on a higher ballot, so the omission is a path asymmetry rather than a uniformly absent mechanism.
unknowns: Whether a higher-ballot AcceptReply can legally arrive while lb.status == ACCEPTED at the coordinator's ballot (concurrent recovery of the same instance).
Whether the resulting non-completion is always bounded by the executeCommands recovery timer.
Whether IsLeader gating leaves a non-leader coordinator with any escalation route.
question.trigger_rationale: A structurally parallel pair of handlers treats a higher-ballot reply differently, and the Accept one is unreachable because of an earlier equality guard; that is a concrete progress mechanism whose premise (legality of the concurrent higher-ballot reply) is worth resolving before claiming a defect.
